exposure: Anti-tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF) therapy continuation beyond week 30 of pregnancy
Anti-TNF therapy discontinuation before week 25 of pregnancy
outcome: Relapse rate of IBD after week 22 of pregnancy
Loss of response to anti-TNF therapy in mothers
Birth outcomes (birth weight, gestational age at delivery, mode of delivery, breastfeeding rates)
Infant growth, infection rate, allergies, eczema, and adverse reactions to vaccines at 1 year of age
cohort: 106 pregnant women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with 83 completed pregnancies
finding: Discontinuing anti-TNF therapy in the second trimester of pregnancy in women with IBD in sustained remission did not lead to increased risks for mothers or their children compared to continuing treatment.
birth_weight: Lower birth weight observed in infants of mothers with IBD compared to controls
